analyst_view.overall: Early view: Betis host Rayo at La Cartuja four days after a Champions League trip to Slovan Bratislava. Pellegrini has said his squad is deep enough to rotate, and Cucho Hernández should be close to fitness by then. Rayo under Beñat San José press hard and play open games; they come off a home match with Valencia amid continuing fan protests at Vallecas.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Betis have attackers to spare (Isco, Antony, Abde, Riquelme and possibly Cucho back), and San José's Rayo conceded heavily early in the season and still play a high-pressing, open game. I lean towards three goals.

corners.text: The site expects 10.4 corners. Betis took eight corners at Elche and shoot a lot from distance, while Rayo won six even in defeat at Anoeta. Both teams attack down the flanks, which points slightly higher.

cards.text: The model has 5.4 cards, 3.3 of them for Rayo, which looks heavy. Rayo took two yellows at Real Sociedad and Betis none at Elche. Without derby or relegation tension, four or five cards seems more likely.

shots.text: The site expects 31.1 shots, which fits. Betis had 18 at Elche and Rayo pressed well enough to take 11 at Anoeta, but some rotation after Bratislava may take a bit off Betis' output.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. Many of Betis' shots are speculative (Antony had gone more than 30 league shots without a goal by late October), and a rotated side may be less sharp. Eight or nine seems right.
